The budgetary allocation towards roads and bridges for FY 2026-27 stands at approximately ₹1.22 lakh crore, about 5 per cent higher than the revised estimates for FY 2025- 26, underscoring the Government's continued commitment to the sector.

The Government has also intensified its asset monetisation programme, having cumulatively monetised over ₹1.5 lakh crore of highway assets through Toll-Operate-Transfer (TOT), Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvIT) and securitisation, with a target of ₹30,000 crore for FY 2025-26 alone.
Growth & demand: Our primary objective in the coming years will be to build a healthy and sustainable order book, which will provide revenue visibility and restore growth momentum.

The Company believes that sustainable and long-term growth of every stakeholder depends upon the judicious and effective use of available resources and consistent endeavor to achieve excellence in business along with active participation in the growth of society, building of environmental balances and significant contribution in economic growth.

The Government of India's continued emphasis on infrastructure-led growth - through the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan, the National Infrastructure Pipeline and enhanced budgetary allocations - has created a strong multiplier effect across the construction and allied sectors.
